_doc: Structured large-load tariff terms, one row per tariff or schedule. These figures previously existed only inside prose in the Takeaway column, which made the single most decision-useful comparison in the tracker — what a developer actually signs up to in each territory — impossible to render. A null means the term was NOT stated in what was read, never that it does not exist. Do not fill a null by inference from a neighbouring tariff.

fields.threshold_mw: Minimum demand at which the schedule applies or becomes mandatory.
fields.load_factor_pct: Minimum monthly load factor required for eligibility, where the schedule imposes one.
fields.term_years: Initial contract term. See term_note for whether a ramp period is included.
fields.ramp_years: Maximum ramp period, where stated separately.
fields.min_take_pct: Minimum billing demand as a percentage of contract or contracted demand — the take-or-pay floor.
fields.notice_months: Notice required to terminate or materially reduce contracted capacity.
fields.exit_fee: Whether an exit or termination charge applies.
fields.status: Where the tariff stands as of 2026-09-18.

data.tariff: Rate No. 50 — High Load Factor Power Service
data.collateral: Credit security unless the offtaker or guarantor holds two of three A-/A3 ratings
data.term_note: 20-year minimum initial term on a Commission-filed ESA. Transmission-voltage service into a dedicated substation. 80% billing demand floor plus an 80% summer ratchet.

data.collateral: Up to two years of minimum bills
data.term_note: 12-year base term plus a ramp of up to 5 years, so 12-17 years in total. Base demand rates set 50% above the standard Industrial and Large Power rate; all-in bills run 8-10% above it. A Bring Your Own Generation path preserves the SB-98 sales-tax exemption.

data.collateral: Two years of minimum monthly bills
data.term_note: 12-year term after ramp. Base rate approximately $0.062/kWh. 65% customer share of earnings above the allowed ROE.

data.tariff: Schedule L.P.S. — large load special terms and conditions
data.collateral: Cash collateral accruing interest; no freely negotiated alternative permitted
data.term_note: Applies at 100 MW at a single site or 150 MW aggregated, for load added after 1 July 2025. 14-year initial term INCLUSIVE of a ramp of up to four years. 42 months' notice to terminate or cut capacity by more than 20%. Exit fee carries a defined mitigation and dispute-resolution path. A separate large-load rate class was expressly found not to be required.
data.status: Final order 2026-06-01; under appeal by the Retail Energy Advancement League

data.term_note: 85% of contracted transmission and distribution demand, 60% of generation demand. Takes effect 2027-01-01. Six customers elected under 2026 Va. Acts ch. 1124 to remain on GS-4. Cost allocation was settled separately in Rider T1, PUR-2026-00056. The compliance filing is due at least 45 days before the effective date and rates should not be modelled before it lands.

data.tariff: Schedules LP-1, DPS, HV-1 and HV-2 — revised terms and conditions
data.term_note: NOVEC states the revisions are aimed at insulating other members from large-load costs and proposes no change to the rates themselves. The specific terms were not read. Live on an interim basis from 2026-09-01 and modifiable at hearing, so anything signed before April 2027 is signed against provisional terms.
data.status: In effect on an interim basis from 2026-09-01; hearing 2027-04-21

data.tariff: Rate Schedule XHLF — Extra High Load Factor
data.term_note: MANDATORY, plus an executed Load Commitment Agreement, for large high-load-factor customers beginning service after 1 January 2024 and not covered by the June 2025 resource plan. APS argues existing Service Schedule 1 already lets it impose these terms without separate Commission pre-approval, so they are effectively non-negotiable. The MW threshold and minimum-take percentage were NOT established — exhibit APS-54 needs a direct read to close this.
data.status: Hearings concluded June 2026; reply briefs 2026-09-11; awaiting a Recommended Opinion and Order

data.tariff: Panasonic special contract (outside the LLPS tariff)
data.term_note: The comparison point for anything negotiated outside the standard tariff. Minimum-bill provisions the Utilities Director called the most robust he had reviewed. Discounts confined strictly to base rates — nothing off the fuel, property-tax or transmission delivery riders.

data.tariff: Company contracting standard (not a filed tariff)
data.collateral: Robust credit terms; contributions in aid of construction during heavy investment
data.term_note: Stated as 15-20 year terms with minimum bills and an early termination fee to recoup unrecovered costs. This is Entergy's described contracting practice from its 2026 Investor Day, NOT a filed tariff, and the terms are therefore indicative rather than binding on the Commission.

data.tariff: Customer Protection Plus (framework; tariff filing pending)
data.term_note: Duke discloses the mechanism categories — minimum billing, termination damages and collateral — but no numbers. The formal North Carolina tariff filing is due 2026-09-30 and should replace this row with real figures.

convergence_note: Across the six tariffs with a stated threshold and term, the cluster is tight: threshold 25-100 MW, term 10-20 years, minimum take 80-85%, collateral around two years of minimum bills, notice 24-42 months. Treat a DEVIATION from this cluster as the newsworthy thing, not the cluster itself. The legislative template moving through the states tracks it closely at 50-150 MW, 75-85% minimum take and 10-15 year terms.
known_gaps: APS XHLF — threshold and minimum take not established; read exhibit APS-54 in E-01345A-25-0105.
NOVEC — the revised terms themselves were not read, only the order docketing them.
Duke NC — no numbers until the 2026-09-30 filing.
OG&E — a tariff reported as 'Extra Large Power & Light' is unconfirmed while the Oklahoma portal returns HTTP 500. Deliberately absent from this table rather than entered on report.
Georgia Power, Alabama Power, AEP Ohio, ComEd, PPL, SWEPCO, Oncor — large-load tariffs exist or are in progress but their terms have not been extracted into this table.
